category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: Identify the specific nerve that distributes postganglionic secretomotor fibers from the otic ganglion to the parotid gland.
back:
• Auriculotemporal Nerve
• This is a branch of the Mandibular division of Trigeminal (V3).

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: The submandibular ganglion is anatomically suspended from the [___] nerve as it crosses the hyoglossus muscle.
back:
• Lingual Nerve
• It is attached by two short communicating branches.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: A patient presents with dry mouth and reduced salivation after a deep floor-of-mouth laceration involving the lingual nerve. Which glands are affected by the disruption of this ganglion's distribution?
back:
• Submandibular gland
• Sublingual gland
• Small mucous glands of the oral floor.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: Describe the functional role of the Lesser Petrosal nerve in the secretomotor pathway of the parotid gland.
back:
• Carries preganglionic parasympathetic fibers from the tympanic plexus (CN IX).
• Exits middle ear → passes through foramen ovale → synapses in Otic ganglion.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
coreConcept: Sympathetic Roots of Head and Neck Ganglia
front: Contrast the sympathetic roots of the otic and submandibular ganglia regarding their vascular source.
back:
• Otic: Sympathetic plexus surrounding the Middle Meningeal Artery.
• Submandibular: Sympathetic plexus surrounding the Facial Artery.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: Specify the exact location of the submandibular ganglion relative to the submandibular salivary gland.
back:
• Deep to the submandibular gland
• Located on the lateral surface of the hyoglossus muscle.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: The otic ganglion is situated in the infratemporal fossa, located immediately inferior to the [___] and medial to the mandibular nerve (V3).
back:
• Foramen ovale.
• It is functionally associated with the glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX).
• It is physically related to the trunk of the mandibular nerve.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: A surgeon is performing a dissection in the submandibular triangle. He identifies a small ganglion suspended from the lingual nerve on the surface of the hyoglossus muscle. Identify this structure and its functional roots.
back:
• Submandibular Ganglion.
• Parasympathetic root: Chorda tympani (via lingual nerve).
• Sympathetic root: Plexus on the facial artery.
• Sensory root: Lingual nerve.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: Explain the parasympathetic secretomotor pathway to the parotid gland, specifically identifying the pre-ganglionic and post-ganglionic segments.
back:
• Pre-ganglionic: Lesser petrosal nerve (branch of CN IX).
• Synapse: Otic ganglion.
• Post-ganglionic: Auriculotemporal nerve.
• Target: Parotid salivary gland.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: Contrast the anatomical suspension of the submandibular ganglion with the attachment of the otic ganglion.
back:
• Submandibular: Suspended from the lingual nerve by two short communicating branches.
• Otic: Closely adherent to the nerve to the medial pterygoid (trunk of V3).

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: Identify the specific structures innervated by the post-ganglionic secretomotor fibers originating from the submandibular ganglion.
back:
• Submandibular salivary gland.
• Sublingual salivary gland.
• Small glands in the floor of the mouth.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: The pre-ganglionic parasympathetic fibers that reach the otic ganglion travel via the [___] nerve, which is a branch of the tympanic plexus.
back:
• Lesser petrosal nerve.
• Originates from the glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX).
• Enters the infratemporal fossa through the foramen ovale or a small canaliculus.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: A 45-year-old patient presents with gustatory sweating (Frey's Syndrome) following parotid surgery. This condition arises when parasympathetic fibers from the [___] ganglion misdirect to sweat glands.
back:
• Otic Ganglion.
• Occurs due to aberrant regeneration of secretomotor fibers into the auriculotemporal nerve.
• Fibers normally destined for the parotid gland now supply overlying skin sweat glands.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: Detail the motor fibers that pass through the otic ganglion without synapsing and identify their target muscles.
back:
• Fibers: From the nerve to the medial pterygoid (V3).
• Targets: Tensor veli palatini and Tensor tympani muscles.
• These are somatic motor fibers, not autonomic.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
coreConcept: Sympathetic Roots of Head and Neck Ganglia
front: Distinguish between the sympathetic roots of the otic and submandibular ganglia based on their arterial origins.
back:
• Otic: Derived from the sympathetic plexus around the middle meningeal artery.
• Submandibular: Derived from the sympathetic plexus around the facial artery.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
coreConcept: Nerve Components of the Submandibular Ganglion
front: Identify the nerve that carries taste fibers from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue and joins the lingual nerve in the infratemporal fossa.
back:
• Chorda tympani (CN VII).
• Carries taste and pre-ganglionic parasympathetic fibers to the submandibular ganglion.
• Joins the lingual nerve from behind at an acute angle.

category: Describe the bony features and muscle attachment of mandible
front: The [___] is a sharp, bony projection located on the medial surface of the mandibular ramus, situated immediately anterior to the mandibular foramen, which provides attachment for the sphenomandibular ligament.
back: Lingula. It serves as a vital anatomical landmark for the inferior alveolar nerve block, marking the site where the nerve enters the mandibular canal.

category: Describe the bony features and muscle attachment of mandible
front: A 25-year-old male sustains a blow to the chin. Radiographs reveal a fracture at the neck of the mandible. The [___] muscle, inserting into the pterygoid fovea, is responsible for pulling the condylar fragment anteriorly and medially.
back: Lateral pterygoid muscle. Its attachment to the neck and TMJ capsule causes typical displacement of the proximal fragment, leading to malocclusion and deviation of the jaw.

category: Describe the bony features and muscle attachment of mandible
front: Explain the clinical and functional significance of the mental spines (genial tubercles) located on the internal surface of the mandibular symphysis.
back: - Superior spines: Origin for Genioglossus (protrudes tongue). - Inferior spines: Origin for Geniohyoid (elevates hyoid). - Function: Maintains an open airway by preventing the tongue from falling backward.

category: Describe the bony features and muscle attachment of mandible
front: Contrast the anatomical insertions and primary clinical vulnerabilities of the coronoid process versus the condyloid process of the mandible.
back: - Coronoid: Insertion for Temporalis muscle; rarely fractured. - Condyloid: Articulates at TMJ; insertion for Lateral Pterygoid; the narrow neck is a frequent site for indirect fractures.

category: Describe the bony features and muscle attachment of mandible
front: Identify the specific anatomical target and the clinical landmarks required for the successful needle insertion step of an inferior alveolar nerve block.
back: - Target: Mandibular foramen near the lingula. - Landmarks: Coronoid notch, pteryomandibular raphe, and the occlusal plane. Needle is inserted lateral to the raphe into the pterygomandibular space.

category: Describe the bony features and muscle attachment of mandible
front: In the neonatal mandible, the angle is [___], but it gradually becomes more vertical (approaching 90 degrees) in the adult as the ramus elongates and teeth erupt.
back: Obtuse (approximately 140 to 150 degrees). This morphology changes postnatally as the mandible adapts to the mechanical demands of mastication and dental development.

category: Describe the bony features and muscle attachment of mandible
front: A patient presents with a painful swelling in the floor of the mouth that increases during meals. The physician palpates a stone in the [___] fossa, situated above the mylohyoid line.
back: Sublingual fossa. This area houses the sublingual gland and submandibular duct. Swellings here are often due to sialolithiasis or ranulae, separated from the neck by the mylohyoid muscle.

category: Describe the bony features and muscle attachment of mandible
front: Explain the mechanical difference in displacement between a symphyseal fracture and a condylar neck fracture based on the muscle attachments of the mandible.
back: - Symphyseal: Minimal displacement; bilateral muscles (digastrics) provide balanced tension. - Condylar neck: Significant displacement; the lateral pterygoid pulls the fragment anteriorly and medially, away from the ramus.

category: Describe the bony features and muscle attachment of mandible
front: Contrast the mandibular insertions and the combined mechanical role of the masseter and the medial pterygoid muscles.
back: - Masseter: Lateral surface of the ramus and angle. - Medial Pterygoid: Medial surface of the ramus and angle. - Combined Role: They form a 'mandibular sling' that elevates the jaw.

category: Describe the bony features and muscle attachment of mandible
front: Specify the attachment site and functional significance of the mylohyoid muscle on the internal surface of the mandible.
back: - Attachment: Mylohyoid line. - Significance: Forms the 'diaphragm oris' (muscular floor); separates the sublingual and submandibular spaces; elevates the floor of the mouth during swallowing.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: Postganglionic secretomotor fibers from the otic ganglion reach the parotid gland by hitchhiking on the [___] nerve.
back: • Auriculotemporal nerve (branch of Mandibular nerve/V3).

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: A surgeon performing a submandibular gland excision inadvertently damages the ganglion suspended from the lingual nerve. This will primarily affect secretomotor supply to which glands?
back:
• Submandibular gland.
• Sublingual gland.
• Small salivary glands in the floor of the mouth.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: Trace the path of preganglionic parasympathetic fibers that synapse in the Otic ganglion.
back:
• Origin: Inferior salivary nucleus (CN IX).
• Pathway: Tympanic nerve → Tympanic plexus → Lesser petrosal nerve.
• Exit: Foramen ovale to reach the infratemporal fossa.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: Contrast the Otic and Submandibular ganglia regarding their associated parent nerves and anatomical locations.
back:
• Otic: Medial to Mandibular nerve (V3) in the infratemporal fossa.
• Submandibular: Suspended from the Lingual nerve on the surface of the hyoglossus muscle.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: Identify the cranial nerve that provides the preganglionic parasympathetic root for the submandibular ganglion.
back:
• Facial nerve (CN VII).
• Fibers travel via the Chorda tympani and Lingual nerve.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: The submandibular ganglion is anatomically located on the superficial surface of the [___] muscle.
back: • Hyoglossus muscle.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: A patient develops 'sweating while eating' (Frey’s syndrome) after parotid surgery. Explain the ganglionic origin of the misdirected fibers.
back:
• Parasympathetic fibers from the Otic ganglion.
• Normally travel via the Auriculotemporal nerve.
• Misroute to join the Great Auricular nerve to supply sweat glands.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: Explain the role of the Chorda tympani in the functional dynamics of the submandibular ganglion.
back:
• Carries preganglionic parasympathetic fibers from CN VII.
• Joins Lingual nerve to reach the ganglion.
• Carries taste fibers from anterior 2/3 of tongue (passing through without synapsing).

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: Distinguish between the preganglionic parasympathetic roots of the Otic and Submandibular ganglia.
back:
• Otic: Lesser petrosal nerve (branch of CN IX).
• Submandibular: Chorda tympani nerve (branch of CN VII).

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: Which specific nerve provides the sensory root to the otic ganglion?
back: • Nerve to the medial pterygoid (branch of V3).

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: The otic ganglion is anatomically situated in the infratemporal fossa, located immediately inferior to the [___] and medial to the mandibular nerve.
back:
• Foramen ovale
• Adherent to the nerve to medial pterygoid
• Deep to the mandibular nerve (V3)

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: A patient presents with a lack of parotid secretion after a fracture at the base of the skull involving the lesser petrosal nerve. The preganglionic parasympathetic fibers lost in this case normally synapse in the [___].
back:
• Otic ganglion
• Origin: Inferior salivary nucleus (CN IX)
• Pathway: Tympanic plexus to lesser petrosal nerve

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: Explain the mechanism by which preganglionic parasympathetic fibers reach the submandibular ganglion to initiate salivation.
back:
• Fibers arise from superior salivary nucleus (CN VII)
• Travel via chorda tympani
• Join the lingual nerve in the infratemporal fossa to reach the ganglion

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
coreConcept: Cranial Nerve Origins of Salivary Ganglia
front: Contrast the otic and submandibular ganglia based on the specific cranial nerves providing their preganglionic parasympathetic input.
back:
• Otic Ganglion: Glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX) via lesser petrosal nerve
• Submandibular Ganglion: Facial nerve (CN VII) via chorda tympani

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: Identify the nerve that physically suspends the submandibular ganglion within the submandibular triangle.
back:
• Lingual nerve (branch of V3)
• Ganglion hangs by two short roots
• Positioned on the lateral surface of the hyoglossus muscle

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: Postganglionic secretomotor fibers from the submandibular ganglion primarily distribute to the [___] and [___] salivary glands.
back:
• Submandibular gland
• Sublingual gland
• Also supplies minor glands in the oral floor

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
coreConcept: Clinical Relationship of Lingual Nerve and Submandibular Ganglion
front: Following an aggressive extraction of a lower third molar, a patient loses salivary function in the floor of the mouth. Which anatomical structure was most likely damaged, leading to the disruption of the submandibular ganglion's supply?
back:
• Lingual nerve
• Carries preganglionic fibers (chorda tympani) to the ganglion
• Lies close to the medial surface of the mandible near the last molar

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: Describe how postganglionic parasympathetic fibers from the otic ganglion reach the parotid salivary gland.
back:
• Fibers join the auriculotemporal nerve
• Auriculotemporal nerve (branch of V3) conveys them to the parotid substance

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: Distinguish between the sympathetic roots of the otic and submandibular ganglia.
back:
• Otic: Derived from the plexus on the middle meningeal artery
• Submandibular: Derived from the plexus on the facial artery

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: Identify the sensory root of the otic ganglion.
back:
• Nerve to medial pterygoid
• Sensory fibers pass through the ganglion without synapsing

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: The otic ganglion is a small parasympathetic station located in the infratemporal fossa, situated specifically [___] to the mandibular nerve (V3) just below the foramen ovale.
back:
* Medial aspect of V3.
* It is adherent to the nerve to the medial pterygoid muscle.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: A 45-year-old patient undergoes surgery in the submandibular triangle. Post-operatively, saliva production is diminished. The ganglion responsible for these secretomotor fibers is suspended from which specific nerve?
back:
* Lingual Nerve.
* Suspended by two short filaments.
* Carries preganglionic fibers from the Chorda Tympani (CN VII).

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: Outline the parasympathetic secretomotor pathway for parotid gland secretion, beginning from the brainstem nucleus.
back:
* Nucleus: Inferior Salivary Nucleus (CN IX).
* Preganglionic: Tympanic nerve → Lesser petrosal nerve.
* Synapse: Otic Ganglion.
* Postganglionic: Auriculotemporal nerve (V3).

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: Contrast the preganglionic parasympathetic roots of the otic and submandibular ganglia.
back:
* Otic: Lesser petrosal nerve (from Glossopharyngeal nerve, CN IX).
* Submandibular: Chorda tympani (from Facial nerve, CN VII) hitchhiking via the Lingual nerve.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: Describe the precise anatomical location of the submandibular ganglion relative to the extrinsic tongue muscles.
back:
* Located deep to the submandibular gland.
* Lies on the superficial surface of the hyoglossus muscle.
* Anterior to the deep part of the gland.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: Postganglionic parasympathetic fibers from the otic ganglion reach their target organ by hitchhiking with the [___] nerve.
back:
* Auriculotemporal nerve.
* Target: Parotid salivary gland.
* Origin: Posterior division of Mandibular nerve (V3).

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: A patient presents with gustatory sweating (Frey's syndrome) following parotid surgery. Explain the ganglionic origin of the misdirected fibers.
back:
* Origin: Otic Ganglion.
* Mechanism: Parasympathetic secretomotor fibers meant for parotid gland regrow to join sympathetic fibers in the great auricular/auriculotemporal nerves supplying sweat glands.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: Explain the role of the Chorda tympani nerve in the functional distribution of the submandibular ganglion.
back:
* Provides preganglionic parasympathetic fibers.
* Joins lingual nerve in the infratemporal fossa.
* Synapses in submandibular ganglion to stimulate submandibular and sublingual secretion.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: Distinguish between the sources of the sympathetic roots for the otic and submandibular ganglia.
back:
* Otic: Plexus on the Middle Meningeal Artery.
* Submandibular: Plexus on the Facial Artery.
* Both pass through ganglia without synapsing.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: Which somatic motor branches of the mandibular nerve (V3) pass through the otic ganglion without synapsing?
back:
* Nerve to Tensor Veli Palatini.
* Nerve to Tensor Tympani.
* These arise from the nerve to the medial pterygoid.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: The otic ganglion is located in the infratemporal fossa, specifically situated [___] to the trunk of the mandibular nerve (CN V3).
back:
• Medial
• Positioned just below the foramen ovale
• Adherent to the nerve to the medial pterygoid muscle.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: A patient presents with Frey's syndrome, where eating triggers sweating instead of salivation. This condition results from misdirected fibers of the [___] nerve, which normally carries postganglionic parasympathetic output from the otic ganglion.
back:
• Auriculotemporal nerve
• Carries postganglionic secretomotor fibers
• Targets the parotid salivary gland.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: Describe the relay pathway of the secretomotor root to the submandibular ganglion.
back:
• Preganglionic fibers from the Superior Salivary Nucleus (CN VII)
• Travel via chorda tympani to join the lingual nerve
• Synapse within the submandibular ganglion.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: Contrast the otic and submandibular ganglia regarding their primary anatomical suspension in the head.
back:
• Otic: Topographically related to CN V3 trunk but not suspended by it
• Submandibular: Physically suspended from the lingual nerve by two short roots.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: Identify the specific cranial nerve and branch that provides the preganglionic parasympathetic root to the otic ganglion.
back:
• Glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX)
• Lesser petrosal nerve
• Arises from the tympanic plexus.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: The submandibular ganglion is located on the lateral surface of the [___] muscle, deep to the submandibular salivary gland.
back:
• Hyoglossus muscle
• Suspended from the lingual nerve
• Medial to the body of the mandible.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: A 45-year-old female undergoes surgery in the submandibular triangle. The surgeon accidentally damages the plexus on the facial artery. Predict the autonomic loss to the submandibular ganglion.
back:
• Loss of the sympathetic root
• Postganglionic fibers from the superior cervical ganglion
• Results in altered vasomotor control to the glands.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: Explain the biological pathway of postganglionic fibers from the submandibular ganglion.
back:
• Direct branches to the submandibular gland
• Re-entry into the lingual nerve to reach the sublingual gland
• Provides secretomotor innervation to both glands.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: Distinguish between the sympathetic roots of the otic and submandibular ganglia based on their arterial source.
back:
• Otic: Plexus on the middle meningeal artery
• Submandibular: Plexus on the facial artery
• Both carry postganglionic fibers from the superior cervical ganglion.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: Which specific branch of the mandibular nerve (CN V3) provides the sensory root to the otic ganglion?
back:
• Nerve to the medial pterygoid
• Sensory fibers pass through the ganglion without synapsing
• Supplies the parotid gland capsule.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: Preganglionic parasympathetic fibers reaching the otic ganglion originate from the glossopharyngeal nerve and travel via the [___] nerve.
back:
* Lesser petrosal nerve
* Originates from the tympanic plexus
* Leaves the skull via foramen ovale or canaliculus innominatus.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: A patient develops localized sweating and flushing on the cheek while eating after a parotid gland injury. This 'gustatory sweating' involves misdirected fibers that normally relay in the [___] ganglion.
back:
* Otic ganglion
* Pathophysiology: Auriculotemporal nerve parasympathetic fibers misroute to sweat glands (Frey's Syndrome).

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: Explain how preganglionic secretomotor fibers from the facial nerve reach the submandibular ganglion.
back:
* Travel via chorda tympani nerve
* Exit petrotympanic fissure to join lingual nerve
* Hitchhike with lingual nerve to the ganglion.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: A surgeon operating on the floor of the mouth must identify a small ganglion suspended from the lingual nerve. This structure is located on the surface of the [___] muscle.
back:
* Hyoglossus muscle
* It is located deep to the submandibular gland
* Connected to lingual nerve by two short roots.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: List the secretomotor distribution of the postganglionic fibers arising from the submandibular ganglion.
back:
* Submandibular salivary gland
* Sublingual salivary gland
* Minor lingual and floor-of-mouth glands.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: The otic ganglion is anatomically located in the infratemporal fossa, immediately medial to the [___] nerve just below the foramen ovale.
back:
* Mandibular nerve (V3)
* Specifically adherent to the nerve to the medial pterygoid muscle.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: A lesion of the lesser petrosal nerve would specifically result in the loss of secretomotor function to which gland?
back:
* Parotid gland
* Pathway: Lesser petrosal nerve → Otic ganglion → Auriculotemporal nerve → Parotid gland.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: Describe the source and route of the sympathetic fibers that pass through the otic ganglion.
back:
* Source: Superior cervical ganglion
* Route: Plexus around the middle meningeal artery
* Result: Vasoconstriction (fibers do not synapse in the ganglion).

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: Contrast the sympathetic roots of the otic and submandibular ganglia regarding the specific arteries they follow.
back:
* Otic: Follows the middle meningeal artery plexus
* Submandibular: Follows the facial artery plexus.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: Which cranial nerve provides the sensory root to the submandibular ganglion?
back:
* Trigeminal nerve (Mandibular division, V3)
* Specifically via the lingual nerve
* Fibers pass through without synapsing.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: The preganglionic parasympathetic fibers reaching the otic ganglion originate from the inferior salivary nucleus of the [___] nerve.
back:
• Glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX).
• Fibers travel via the tympanic plexus.
• Emerge from the middle ear as the lesser petrosal nerve.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
coreConcept: Clinical Correlation of Otic Ganglion Distribution
front: A patient experiences 'Frey’s Syndrome,' where the skin over the parotid gland sweats during meals. This occurs because parasympathetic fibers intended for the otic ganglion misroute to the [___].
back:
• Auriculotemporal nerve (branch of V3).
• Secretomotor fibers re-innervate cutaneous sweat glands.
• Results from trauma or parotid surgery healing complications.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: Explain the mechanical role of the lingual nerve in the anatomy of the submandibular ganglion.
back:
• The ganglion is physically suspended from the lingual nerve.
• It receives preganglionic fibers (via chorda tympani) through this connection.
• It provides a pathway for postganglionic distribution to the sublingual gland.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
coreConcept: Cranial Nerve Origins of Parasympathetic Ganglia
front: Contrast the otic and submandibular ganglia regarding the cranial nerve source of their preganglionic parasympathetic roots.
back:
• Otic Ganglion: Glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX) via lesser petrosal nerve.
• Submandibular Ganglion: Facial nerve (CN VII) via chorda tympani.
• Both rely on Trigeminal (V) branches for final distribution.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: Identify the specific anatomical location of the otic ganglion within the skull.
back:
• Infratemporal fossa.
• Medial to the mandibular nerve (V3).
• Immediately below the foramen ovale.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: The postganglionic secretomotor fibers from the submandibular ganglion primarily distribute to the [___] and [___] salivary glands.
back:
• Submandibular gland.
• Sublingual gland.
• Small glands in the floor of the mouth.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: A patient presents with a dry mouth (xerostomia) after a deep laceration to the floor of the mouth. If the submandibular ganglion is intact but its preganglionic input is severed, which specific nerve branch is damaged?
back:
• Chorda tympani nerve.
• It carries parasympathetic fibers from CN VII.
• It joins the lingual nerve before reaching the ganglion.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: Describe the physiological transit of sympathetic fibers through the otic ganglion.
back:
• Originate from superior cervical ganglion.
• Travel via the plexus on the middle meningeal artery.
• Pass through the otic ganglion without synapsing to reach the parotid.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: Distinguish between the lesser petrosal nerve and the auriculotemporal nerve in the context of the otic ganglion.
back:
• Lesser Petrosal: Preganglionic input (CN IX) to the ganglion.
• Auriculotemporal: Postganglionic output (V3) from the ganglion to the parotid.
• One brings the signal; the other delivers it.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: State the anatomical relationship of the submandibular ganglion to the hyoglossus muscle.
back:
• The ganglion lies on the superficial surface of the hyoglossus muscle.
• It is situated superior to the submandibular duct.
• It is medial to the body of the mandible.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
coreConcept: Topographical Anatomy of the Otic Ganglion
front: The otic ganglion is a peripheral parasympathetic ganglion located in the infratemporal fossa, situated immediately inferior to the [___].
back: Foramen ovale (medial to the mandibular nerve).

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
coreConcept: Secretomotor Distribution of the Otic Ganglion
front: A patient experiences gustatory sweating (Frey's syndrome) after parotid surgery. This occurs when parasympathetic fibers from the [___] ganglion incorrectly re-innervate skin sweat glands.
back: Otic ganglion (via the auriculotemporal nerve).

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
coreConcept: Parasympathetic Pathway of the Submandibular Ganglion
front: Explain the pathway of preganglionic parasympathetic fibers reaching the submandibular ganglion.
back:
• Origin: Superior salivatory nucleus (CN VII).
• Course: Nervus intermedius to Chorda tympani.
• Transport: Hitchhikes with the lingual nerve to the ganglion.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: Contrast the preganglionic parasympathetic roots of the otic and submandibular ganglia.
back:
• Otic: Lesser petrosal nerve (branch of CN IX).
• Submandibular: Chorda tympani (branch of CN VII) via lingual nerve.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
coreConcept: Anatomical Relations of the Submandibular Ganglion
front: Identify the specific muscle upon which the submandibular ganglion is physically situated and the nerve it is suspended from.
back:
• Muscle: Hyoglossus muscle.
• Nerve: Lingual nerve (suspended by two short roots).

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: Postganglionic secretomotor fibers from the otic ganglion reach the parotid gland by hitchhiking along the [___] nerve.
back: Auriculotemporal nerve (branch of the Mandibular nerve/V3).

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
coreConcept: Functional Distribution of the Submandibular Ganglion
front: A 45-year-old female presents with xerostomia limited to the floor of the mouth. A lesion is suspected at the submandibular ganglion. List the specific glands affected.
back:
• Submandibular salivary gland.
• Sublingual salivary gland.
• Small glands in the floor of the mouth.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
coreConcept: Non-Synaptic Relations of the Otic Ganglion
front: Describe the anatomical relationship between the otic ganglion and the nerve to the medial pterygoid.
back:
• The ganglion is closely adherent to the nerve.
• Fibers to the medial pterygoid, tensor tympani, and tensor veli palatini pass through without synapsing.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
front: Distinguish the sympathetic roots of the otic ganglion from those of the submandibular ganglion based on their arterial source.
back:
• Otic: Plexus around the Middle Meningeal Artery.
• Submandibular: Plexus around the Facial Artery.

category: Describe the location, roots and distribution of otic and submandibular ganglia
coreConcept: Sensory Root of the Submandibular Ganglion
front: Which specific cranial nerve carries the sensory root fibers that pass through the submandibular ganglion?
back: Lingual nerve (a branch of the Mandibular division of Trigeminal Nerve, CN V3).
